description: Set up a first-month budget that survives currency surprises and one-off setup costs.

steps.detail: List tuition deposit, rent deposit, bedding, SIM card, transport card — the first month always costs 30-50% more than a normal month.
steps.title: Expect the first month to be expensive

steps.detail: Convert each expected cost into your home currency using the assistant so the total feels real before you arrive.
steps.title: Convert everything to one currency

steps.detail: Set a total monthly limit plus limits for food, transport, and fun. The assistant warns you at 80% and when you breach a limit.
steps.title: Set a total + 3 category limits

steps.detail: Log every expense the day it happens — 30 seconds now beats reconstructing a week of receipts later.
steps.title: Track every expense daily

steps.detail: Mid-month, check the burn-down pace message: 'at this pace you will spend X by month-end' tells you whether to tighten up.
steps.title: Check your pace mid-month

steps.detail: Keep 10% of your monthly budget untouched as a buffer for exchange-rate moves and surprises.
steps.title: Keep a 10% buffer

tips: Pay rent and tuition by card/wire, not cash, so every big expense is traceable.
Review the month-end summary and adjust next month's limits — budgets get smarter every month.
title: Your first-month budget as an international student
